meta.description: Single source of truth for finding status. Statuses are verified against live code at auditedSha, NOT copied from the dated report prose. See audit-reports/README.md.

meta.auditedShaPriorNote: Restamped 2026-08-18 to 59f502aa4 (a real ancestor of origin/staging, NOT the live tip -- see the auditedRef caveat above) from prior auditedSha d67ed76e0a1 (2026-08-12 run), for a monthly light run (/audit-run cadence rule). Discovered during scoping: d67ed76e0a1 is NOT an ancestor of current staging history (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` returns false) -- PR #803, which landed that full run's own commit alongside the 40 findings it produced, squash-merged into staging as f3096a4ce rather than via a traceable merge commit, so the exact feature-branch SHA the prior restamp recorded was orphaned from mainline the moment the PR merged. A naive `git diff d67ed76e0a1...HEAD` therefore returned a false, enormous result (253 files, 486 commits) by comparing across divergent history instead of a clean diff. The correct anchor for 'what changed since the last full run actually merged to staging' is f3096a4ce (found via `git log --grep`, confirmed as a real ancestor of both endpoints), against which the true light-run scope was exactly 1 commit / 1 file (.github/workflows/deploy-cloudrun.yml, PR #805). CORRECTION (dual-review, 2026-08-19): the FIRST version of this restamp incorrectly asserted '59f502aa4 (== origin/staging)'. That was true at the moment the light-run scoping was computed but had already gone stale by the time the register PR was assembled -- staging advanced 7 more commits (43 files, including PR #819 which extended an unrelated pre-existing finding's notes) before this branch was pushed. The false equality claim was caught by BOTH the Codex senior-dev pass and the Claude adversary pass on PR #824's dual review, alongside a separate and more serious defect it enabled: the register PR's first draft was assembled by copying a stale local file over the correctly-checked-out current-staging FINDINGS.json rather than re-deriving the register from current staging via audit-merge.rb, which silently reverted the 7 commits' worth of legitimate concurrent changes to the file -- including 4,197 characters of PR #819's additions to LL-854b1d3853's notes. That defect was NOT a consequence of the auditedSha choice; it was a separate assembly-process error (raw file overwrite instead of a proper merge onto current staging), fixed by rebuilding the register on top of d2bf421f7 and re-running audit-merge.rb before this PR's second push. This is a distinct, previously-undocumented failure mode from the one scripts/audit-merge.rb's --no-restamp flag (branch scot/fix/audit-merge-sha-decoupling, unmerged as of this run) was built to fix -- that work separates the VERIFICATION sha from the AUDIT POINTER for out-of-band finding additions; this issue is that the audit pointer itself can become a non-ancestor SHA purely from how a full-run PR gets merged (squash vs merge-commit), independent of --no-restamp, AND that assembling a register PR by file-copy rather than through audit-merge.rb against the CURRENT base can silently revert unrelated concurrent work no matter how the auditedSha itself is handled. Recommend Scot decide whether future full-run PRs should be merge-committed (not squashed) specifically to keep meta.auditedSha resolvable via ancestry for the next light run's diff-scoping, and standing process guidance for future register PRs: ALWAYS re-derive audit-reports/FINDINGS.json from the current base branch's tip via audit-merge.rb immediately before opening/updating a register PR -- never copy a working-tree file captured earlier in the session, even if that earlier copy is citation-check green, because green only proves the file's OWN evidence resolves, not that the file reflects the current base. Sign-off for the original restamp is Scot's own /audit-run invocation that started this run (skill is user-invoked only); the correction above was applied by the orchestrator in response to dual-review findings, before Scot's merge decision on PR #824. Restamped 2026-08-12 to d67ed76e0a1 (branch scot/feat/code-hygiene-auditor, 1 commit ahead of origin/staging at branch time) from prior auditedSha 20953ab3d5a (2026-07-08 run). This restamp is NOT a clean single-commit reconciliation like the ones below it: the 6-finder full run that produced d67ed76e0a1 verified its own 40 new findings' evidence at that exact SHA (citation-check green), but the ~110 pre-existing findings from before this run keep their OWN original evidence.sha values, unchanged by this restamp -- consistent with this register's standing per-finding-pin design, not a regression. Both still resolve correctly at their pinned evidence.sha (d67ed76e0a1) today; this note exists so a future restamp knows to re-verify those two lines specifically rather than assume the register's overall auditedSha jump means everything was re-verified. Restamped 2026-06-18 to staging tip 59e20439e from prior auditedSha d72463c75 (Scot sign-off 2026-06-18). The only commit between the two is #416, a GCP provisioning fix touching solely scripts/gcp/phase3-data-layer.sh (Memorystore --enable-auth flag + comment); no finding's evidence anchor points at that file, so no finding status could have changed and no new findings surface. Per-finding evidence.sha anchors are unchanged, so citation-check still validates each snippet at its own pinned commit. Prior restamp 2026-06-17 moved 7ed643e92 (scot/test/audit-run-e2e, 2026-06-16) -> d72463c75 after #410/#411/#412/#413 merged.
meta.idAlgorithm: id = 'LL-' + sha256(ruleKey + '|' + path) first 10 hex chars; stable across runs so recurrence is a diff
meta.governance: Only Scot closes a finding, downgrades severity, accepts risk, or sets a disposition (accepted/fixed/dismissed-false-positive/wontfix). closureEvidence.attestation and disposition.decidedBy stay empty until Scot signs. Findings are added mechanically (scripts/audit-merge.rb from /audit-run, scripts/promote-finding.rb from PR-time reviews) and only ever land as status 'open' with disposition 'untriaged'; the adding scripts never close, downgrade, or triage. No student/patient data ever appears here; evidence snippets are code only and any PII/secret-bearing finding is refused at promotion, never redacted-in.
meta.disposition: Optional per-finding triage state, orthogonal to status. status answers 'does the issue still exist in code' (lifecycle, citation-validated); disposition answers 'what did we decide to do about it' (untriaged/accepted/fixed/dismissed-false-positive/wontfix). A finding with no disposition object is treated as untriaged. Set only by Scot.
meta.remediationSLA: critical 24-72h, high 15-30d, medium 60d, low 90d (advisory; from plan section 1.1)

findings.title: Redis connections without TLS; shared across environments

remediation.options: Use TLS (rediss) and per-environment instances. Resolved for the production path by the GCP Memorystore cutover (private VPC, SERVER_AUTHENTICATION transit encryption, AUTH enabled). Non-prod / Render-fallback sharing tracked separately as LL-7314b5a8ea.

closureEvidence.verifierNote: Verified live 2026-07-22 against the post-cutover production stack (GCP project lingolinq-prod), four independent checks: (1) Memorystore instance lingolinq-prod-redis reports transitEncryptionMode=SERVER_AUTHENTICATION, authEnabled=True, connectMode=PRIVATE_SERVICE_ACCESS, host 10.160.1.3 port 6378 (TLS port) [gcloud redis instances list --region=us-central1]. (2) Secret Manager REDIS_URL resolves to scheme=rediss host=10.160.1.3 port=6378 with AUTH credentials (credentials not recorded). (3) Code path: RedisInit.redis_options sets :ssl=>true and :ssl_params for a rediss:// URI, and redis_ssl_params builds an OpenSSL::X509::Store from REDIS_CA_CERT with VERIFY_PEER on (config/initializers/resque.rb:16-23, :35+); REDIS_CA_CERT is mounted on the lingolinq-web service. verify_hostname is off (REDIS_TLS_VERIFY_HOSTNAME=false) because Memorystore presents an instance-scoped cert while redis-client sets SNI to the private IP; CA-chain verification remains enforced. (4) Live probe: Cloud Run job lingolinq-redischeck execution lingolinq-redischeck-l5skk (2026-07-22) returned REDIS_PING=PONG, REDIS_RW=ok, CA_BLOCKS=1 -- a successful PING over rediss:// proves the TLS handshake completed against the supplied CA, so this is TLS-in-force, not capability-only. Dedicated-instance half: lingolinq-prod-redis is the only Memorystore instance in the project and is reachable only from the prod VPC, so the production path is no longer shared with staging/dev. RESIDUAL (not part of this closure): Render still runs exactly one Key Value instance, lingolinq-redis (red-d46rhqer433s738dha9g), shared by lingolinq-prod, lingolinq-staging, lingolinq-dev and PR previews, over plaintext redis://. lingolinq-prod web on Render is still un-suspended as the cutover rollback fallback. Tracked as LL-7314b5a8ea; a rollback to Render re-exposes the production path until Render is decommissioned.
closureEvidence.attestation: Scot Wahlquist 2026-07-22: attested verified-closed for the production path; Memorystore cutover verified live (rediss://, SERVER_AUTHENTICATION, AUTH enabled, private VPC, PONG over a CA-verified handshake). Render residual carried as LL-7314b5a8ea.

findings.notes: Verified still open 2026-06-12: Redis.new without ssl options (resque.rb:23,26,60,110). NOTE: prod Redis is moving to GCP Memorystore over private VPC (project_render_cloud_migration Phase 3); resolution should land with that cutover. | 2026-06-17 reconcile (staging tip d72463c75, RULE #0 re-verified): #410 shipped the app-side TLS CAPABILITY but NOT live closure. redis_options now enables :ssl + :ssl_params for rediss:// URIs (config/initializers/resque.rb:16-21; redis_ssl_params at :35) and every Redis.new routes through redis_options (resque.rb:79,82,116,166). A plain redis:// URI returns the option hash with no :ssl key, so live Render Redis remains plaintext (resque.rb:12 comment: 'the Render environment is unchanged'). Enabler only; NOT verified-closed. Full closure gated on the GCP Memorystore cutover (Cloud Run migration Phase 3). Disposition (Scot 2026-06-17): keep open / severity high; do not close until the rediss:// cutover lands. | LIVE CHECK 2026-06-21 (render-MCP list_key_value): managed lingolinq-redis (red-d46rhqer433s738dha9g, starter plan, ipAllowList=null) present; instance metadata does not expose the REDIS_URL scheme, so TLS-in-force is unconfirmed. Consistent with enabler-only status; remains open, gated on the Memorystore cutover. | CLOSURE 2026-07-22 (post-cutover): the closure condition recorded in the 2026-06-18 disposition ("full closure lands at the GCP Memorystore cutover") is met. findings.title: Production Postgres (lingolinq-prod-db) reachable from an all-addresses /0 allowlist (public internet)

evidence.snippet: Both Render Postgres instances (incl. the prod DB and the dev/staging DB) report ipAllowList = a single all-addresses /0 entry ('everywhere'), i.e. the database accepts TCP connections from any source IP on the public internet. No source-IP restriction is in effect. render.yaml databases block (render.yaml:101-105) declares no ipAllowList, so the public-everywhere default is the effective committed posture and is not documented as intentional in render.yaml or docs/INFRASTRUCTURE.md. Checked: ipAllowList field only; no secrets/connection strings/PII read or echoed.

remediation.options: Restrict the Render Postgres ipAllowList to known egress sources (the Render service private network / specific NAT egress CIDRs) instead of the all-addresses /0 default, via the database's Access Control settings or an ipAllowList block in render.yaml. Combined with sslmode=require (LL-ba0585ab93, no cert verification), a public-reachable DB is a real network attack surface for a credential-stuffing / brute-force path against the DB. The GCP Cloud SQL cutover removes public DB exposure entirely (private VPC + Cloud SQL connector), so for prod this reconciles with the migration rather than being fixed twice; the dev/staging DB should be restricted now regardless. Until cutover, set an allowlist or accept-risk with a dated note.

findings.title: lingolinq-worker's 512Mi memory limit is too small for ButtonImage/BoardDownstreamButtonSet jobs, causing continuous OOM kills that land as Resque::Failure instead of being requeued

evidence.source: Resque::Failure crosstab (klass x error category) via a throwaway lingolinq-diagcheck3 Cloud Run Job, cross-referenced against gcloud logging read on resource.type=cloud_run_worker_pool for lingolinq-worker, 2026-07-03. Superseded an earlier draft of this finding that incorrectly attributed the failures to the worker-pool scale-down transition (Codex review of PR #516 caught the arithmetic - 833 could not be a subset of 740 new failures - and the unverified crosstab claim).
evidence.snippet: Verified crosstab of all 914 Resque::Failure entries by job-class|error-category: 713 ButtonImage|SIGKILL, 113 BoardDownstreamButtonSet|SIGKILL, 58 BoardDownstreamButtonSet|s3_xml_error (tracked separately as LL-705b10bcd7), 16 ButtonImage|identify_missing (tracked separately as LL-5954bcbbe6), 4 User|SIGKILL, 3 Board|stash_not_found, 2 WordData|still_processing, 2 ButtonImage|SIGSEGV, 2 ButtonImage|still_processing, 1 Board|method_not_found (sum=914, matches Resque::Failure.count exactly). The SIGKILL/SIGSEGV total is 830+2=832. A histogram of SIGKILL/SIGSEGV failed_at timestamps by hour shows they are NOT clustered around the ~00:38-01:30 UTC worker-pool scale-8-to-1 transition: they span 2026-07-03 01h through 15h UTC continuously (e.g. 85 in the 03h bucket, 130 in the 06h bucket, 169 in the 14h bucket - hours after the pool had already returned to manualInstanceCount: 1). Root cause confirmed directly: gcloud logging read on resource.type=cloud_run_worker_pool/lingolinq-worker returns 833 'Out-of-memory event detected in container' log lines in the trailing 24h (2026-07-03T02:46:03Z to 2026-07-03T15:44:14Z), matching the SIGKILL/SIGSEGV count almost exactly. The worker pool's container resource limit is memory: 512Mi (gcloud beta run worker-pools describe lingolinq-worker). This is a standing capacity/sizing problem, not a one-time scale-transition artifact.

remediation.options: Increase the lingolinq-worker worker-pool's memory limit (gcloud beta run worker-pools update lingolinq-worker --memory=1Gi or 2Gi, or the equivalent in the deploy-cloudrun.yml workflow) so forked ButtonImage/BoardDownstreamButtonSet job processes (which shell out to ImageMagick) have enough headroom, then re-verify Resque::Failure.count stops accumulating this error under normal load. findings.title: BoardDownstreamButtonSet S3 writes fail against KMS-encrypted bucket: 'Requests specifying Server Side Encryption with AWS KMS managed keys require AWS Signature Version 4'

evidence.source: Resque::Failure diagnostics via a throwaway lingolinq-diagcheck2 Cloud Run Job (rails runner, cloned from lingolinq-web's image/SA/VPC/Cloud SQL/secrets), 2026-07-03
evidence.snippet: 58 of 914 Resque::Failure entries are BoardDownstreamButtonSet#perform_action failing with the raw S3 API error body: 'InvalidArgumentRequests specifying Server Side Encryption with AWS KMS managed keys require AWS Signature Version 4.Authorization...'. Traced to the actual upload path: lib/uploader.rb Uploader.remote_upload (line 46) calls remote_upload_params (line 293), which hand-builds a browser-style S3 POST policy signed with SigV2 (AWSAccessKeyId + base64 policy + HMAC-SHA1 signature via OpenSSL::HMAC.digest('sha1', ...), lines 296-334) and posts it directly with Typhoeus.post (line 68) - this path does not go through Aws::S3::Client at all, so an aws-sdk-s3 signature_version config has no effect on it. This is a genuine request-signing misconfiguration, independent of the OOM-driven SIGKILL failures (LL-a95e9c5f7c) and independent of the pre-existing ImageMagick/job_stash failures (LL-5954bcbbe6).

remediation.options: Codex review of PR #516 correctly caught two rounds of an inaccurate fix here: first, that the original remediation (bump signature_version on an Aws::S3::Client) targets a client this code path never uses; second, that the corrected suggestion (Aws::S3::Presigner#presigned_post) names a method that doesn't exist on the installed aws-sdk-s3 1.219.0 - Presigner only exposes presigned_url/presigned_request. POST-policy signing lives on the separate Aws::S3::PresignedPost class (lib/aws-sdk-s3/presigned_post.rb), normally reached via the Aws::S3::Bucket resource's presigned_post(options) method (lib/aws-sdk-s3/customizations/bucket.rb:126-133), which builds one from the client's credentials/region/bucket name. Replace the handcrafted SigV2 POST policy in Uploader.remote_upload_params (lib/uploader.rb:293-336) with a PresignedPost built this way (either via Aws::S3::Resource.new(...).bucket(name).presigned_post(...) or Aws::S3::PresignedPost.new(credentials, region, bucket_name, options) directly) - it produces the same browser-postable form-field shape (key/policy/x-amz-* fields) but signed AWS4-HMAC-SHA256, satisfying the KMS-SSE bucket's SigV4 requirement. Verify against the bucket's policy that SSE-KMS enforcement is intended, then re-run the affected board's button-set update and confirm Resque::Failure stops accumulating this error.

closureEvidence.verifierNote: Code-remediated on scot/fix/worker-pool-oom-sigv4: Uploader.remote_upload_params (lib/uploader.rb:293-336, formerly hand-signed SigV2) rewritten to build an Aws::S3::PresignedPost(credentials, region, bucket_name, key:, content_type:, content_length_range:, success_action_status:, acl:) directly, producing an AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-signed POST policy (x-amz-credential/x-amz-algorithm/x-amz-date/x-amz-signature fields) that satisfies SSE-KMS buckets' SigV4 requirement, exactly matching the remediation option's guidance (Aws::S3::PresignedPost, not the nonexistent Presigner#presigned_post). Codex review of this PR (#521) caught a follow-on regression in the first pass (commit 77233fb19): returning the PresignedPost's own regional endpoint as upload_url broke every consumer that pattern-matches a stored self.url against the static global s3.amazonaws.com form (valid_import_bundle_url?, removable_remote_url?, fronted_url, remote_remove, and every *_controller.rb upload_success action). Fixed in afe03d2de: remote_upload_params now returns both upload_url (unchanged canonical global form, for URL construction/matching) and a new post_url (the regional SigV4 POST target); the three Typhoeus.post call sites and two frontend POST targets (content-grabbers.js, beta-feedback-form.js, with a post_url || upload_url fallback) now use post_url. spec/lib/uploader_spec.rb and spec/models/concerns/uploadable_spec.rb updated to assert the split shape; full uploader/uploadable/button_sound/beta_feedback_recording/extra_data/logs/sounds spec suites green except two pre-existing unrelated test-DB-pollution failures (ButtonImage.count inflated by orphaned committed rows; an unrelated GoSecure OpenSSL 'bad decrypt' on cached_copy; a boards_controller_spec BoardLocale.count leak - all three reproduce in isolation on main, unrelated to this change). Not yet live-verified: requires redeploying the rehearsal image and confirming Resque::Failure stops accumulating the KMS-SSE SigV4 error on the next BoardDownstreamButtonSet run, plus a bucket-policy check that SSE-KMS enforcement on this bucket is actually intended. LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-05 on the GCP rehearsal stack: root cause was three stacked AWS-side blockers on lingolinq-prod-uploads (SSE-KMS default encryption with CMK d5a1a377-8f55-469d-a0ab-4a86481dba67 + BucketOwnerEnforced + Block Public Access), not residual code error. Fixes applied with Scot's approval: IAM policy lingolinq-cloudrun-s3-ses v2 (adds kms:GenerateDataKey/kms:Decrypt on the CMK, matching scripts/gcp/iam/lingolinq-cloudrun-s3-ses-policy.json) set as default for user lingolinq-cloudrun-prod; UPLOADS_S3_NO_ACL=1 applied live to lingolinq-web (rev 00003-5t9) and the lingolinq-worker pool and added to deploy-cloudrun.yml via PR #531. End-to-end synthetic verification: a real ButtonImage (id 840) processed by the live worker pool landed in the bucket (224566 bytes, image/png, ServerSideEncryption aws:kms under the expected CMK); record destroy also removed the S3 object. Read path: CloudFront distribution E2X2HAS6Y1L2MI (OAC, bucket-policy + KMS key-policy grants scoped to the distribution ARN) fronts the bucket; UPLOADS_S3_CDN set on both stacks 2026-07-05. Awaiting Scot's verified-closed call. Independently re-confirmed 2026-07-09: same full-failure-log scan used to verify LL-a95e9c5f7c also covers this finding's KMS-SSE SigV4 error class -- NEW_SINCE_DEPLOY=0 since 2026-07-04T22:00:00Z, no new S3 InvalidArgument/SigV4 failures. Still awaiting Scot's verified-closed call.

evidence.source: Resque::Failure diagnostics via a throwaway lingolinq-diagcheck2 Cloud Run Job (rails runner, cloned from lingolinq-web's image/SA/VPC/Cloud SQL/secrets), 2026-07-03
evidence.snippet: Of the 174 Resque::Failure entries present as of 2026-07-03 before the queue:default/queue:slow backlog finished draining (all dated 2026-06-29, unrelated to the later scale-to-8 event): 16 are ButtonImage#perform_action(upload_to_remote) failing 'No such file or directory - identify', indicating the ImageMagick identify binary is missing or misconfigured in the Cloud Run web/worker image; 3 are Board#perform_action(update_setting, \"job_stash\", \"1_1\"/\"1_2\"/\"1_3\") failing 'stash not found: 1_1' etc; and 1 is Board#perform_action(update_privacy) failing 'method not found: Board:update_privacy', i.e. a queued job referencing a method that no longer exists on the Board model (likely deploy/version skew between when the job was enqueued and the running image).

(c) Board:update_privacy - confirm whether this method was intentionally removed/renamed and whether any current code path can still enqueue a job calling it; if so, that enqueue site needs fixing, not just the failed job.

findings.title: A diagnostic SES send to a personal Gmail address never arrived (inbox or spam); a same-account send to a Workspace-internal address arrived immediately

evidence.source: Two live Aws::SES::Client#send_email diagnostics against the same lingolinq-prod SES account/region (us-west-2), 2026-07-03/04. First: a direct-API send to a personal scotwahlquist@gmail.com address (PR #516/#521 0a rehearsal follow-up) returned a real SES MessageId but the recipient confirmed it never arrived in Inbox or Spam. Second (this finding): a retest send to the Workspace-internal beta@lingolinq.com alias (subject "GCP rehearsal SES diag retest (beta@ alias, direct-api)", MessageId 0101019f2a7d6e11-c08396d5-591f-4c0b-95b3-5a83a49e6d57-000000) landed in scot@lingolinq.com's Inbox (not Spam) within seconds of sending.
evidence.snippet: Live SESv2 GetAccount/GetEmailIdentity checks at time of diagnosis: account ProductionAccessEnabled=true, EnforcementStatus=HEALTHY, TRANSACTIONAL use case approved (Details.ReviewDetails.Status=GRANTED); lingolinq.com domain identity VerificationStatus=SUCCESS, DkimAttributes.Status=SUCCESS (Easy DKIM, RSA_2048_BIT); scotwahlquist@gmail.com is NOT on the account suppression list (GetSuppressedDestination -> NotFoundException). CORRECTION (caught by Codex review of this PR, verified against AWS's own API docs before accepting): GetSendStatistics.DeliveryAttempts is documented as "Number of emails that have been sent" -- an account-wide 15-minute aggregate of SES send attempts, NOT a per-message delivery-to-recipient-MTA confirmation. The 2026-07-03T16:47:00Z data point (2 DeliveryAttempts, 0 Bounces, 0 Complaints, 0 Rejects) only shows SES accepted the API call and recorded no account-wide hard bounce in that window; it does NOT prove Gmail's MTA received or processed this specific message, and does not by itself support a conclusion of Gmail-side filtering over any other cause. A live telemetry check on 2026-07-04 found zero SES configuration sets, Virtual Deliverability Manager disabled, and no identity-level delivery-notification topic for lingolinq.com, so no retained per-message delivery event is available for either diagnostic send. Future per-message delivery confirmation requires an SES configuration set with an event destination that carries per-message records (SNS, Amazon Data Firehose, or EventBridge -- plain CloudWatch only publishes aggregate metrics, not per-message events) or Virtual Deliverability Manager enabled before a new test. Separately (and this part is a genuine, confirmed gap, independent of the delivery-attempts question above): MailFromAttributes has no custom MailFromDomain configured -- SES is using its default amazonses.com bounce/Return-Path domain rather than a lingolinq.com subdomain, so SPF does not align with the From: domain (DKIM alignment alone is presumably covering DMARC today, since the domain already has DMARC aggregate reporting flowing to Google/Microsoft). This is worthwhile SPF-alignment hardening on its own merits, not a proven cause of the non-delivery.

remediation.options: (a) Obtain per-message delivery evidence before assigning root cause: enable an SES configuration set with an event destination that carries per-message delivery/bounce/complaint records -- SNS, Amazon Data Firehose, or EventBridge (plain CloudWatch only publishes aggregate metrics/counts, not per-message events, so it would not satisfy this) -- or enable Virtual Deliverability Manager, then re-run the scotwahlquist@gmail.com send and read the actual event for that specific MessageId. (b) Configure a custom MAIL FROM domain (e.g. mail.lingolinq.com) on the SES domain identity so SPF aligns with the From: domain in addition to DKIM -- worthwhile hardening regardless of whether it turns out to be the cause here. (c) Enable the SES deliverability dashboard (currently off) and/or enroll lingolinq.com in Google Postmaster Tools for real external-Gmail reputation signal. (d) Re-test sends to 2-3 different personal-email providers (Gmail, Outlook.com/Hotmail, Yahoo) to determine whether this is Gmail-specific or a broader personal-inbox gap, using (a)'s per-message tracking so the result is actually conclusive this time.

findings.notes:
Surfaced continuing the Phase 5 rehearsal 0a follow-up (PR #521) after Scot confirmed the original personal-Gmail diagnostic email never arrived. Confidence downgraded medium->low and evidence corrected 2026-07-04 after Codex's review of this PR (running against this finding's initial commit) correctly caught that GetSendStatistics.DeliveryAttempts was being misread as delivery confirmation; verified against AWS's own SendDataPoint API docs before accepting the correction. The confirmed, undisputed fact remains: the original send to scotwahlquist@gmail.com never arrived (inbox or spam checked), while a same-account retest to a Workspace-internal address arrived immediately -- the open question is root cause, not whether a real gap exists. Low severity and no user impact today because prod/staging currently carry no real external users (project note: prod has no real users at cutover) -- all current transactional mail recipients are internal/test accounts. Note this finding's evidence base is a single send to each recipient type (n=1 each way), not a reliability claim about Workspace delivery in general; treat the Workspace-internal send as one clean data point, not a proof that SES-to-Workspace mail is broadly reliable. Revisit before onboarding real school-district/hospital/parent users on personal email providers, since password resets, registration confirmations, and consent notifications going silently missing would be a real support burden and, for consent-related mail specifically, a compliance concern (FERPA/COPPA parental notification). REPRODUCED 2026-07-04 via the actual application code path (Phase 5 step 0a follow-up, scot/docs/phase5-0a-status-v2): all prior evidence used a raw Aws::SES::Client#send_email call, not Rails ActionMailer -- this test partially closes that gap. A throwaway Cloud Run Job ran `ActionMailer::Base.mail(...).deliver_now` (delivery_method: :ses, config/environments/production.rb:116) against the currently-deployed lingolinq-web/worker image, sending to both beta@lingolinq.com and scotwahlquist@gmail.com in the same run. Both calls returned real SES MessageIds via Aws::Rails::SesMailer#deliver! (0101019f2b9c732c-... and 0101019f2b9c73e6-... respectively), confirming ActionMailer's :ses delivery-method adapter is correctly wired end-to-end in this Cloud Run environment (SES_REGION/AWS_REGION resolve, AWS_KEY/AWS_SECRET credentials work, DEFAULT_EMAIL_FROM resolves). CAVEAT (raised by Codex review of this PR, accepted): the test called the generic `ActionMailer::Base.mail(...)` directly rather than a concrete application mailer class (UserMailer/AdminMailer/SubscriptionMailer/SupervisorMailer, app/mailers/*.rb, all ActionMailer::Base subclasses) -- it verifies the SES adapter, credentials, and region wiring, not a real transactional mailer's view template or the exact code path a password-reset or notification email takes. A follow-up test through a concrete mailer class is still needed for full representativeness. Checked actual delivery via the connected Gmail account (scotwahlquist@gmail.com): the beta@lingolinq.com-addressed message arrived (INBOX, not spam) -- note this refines the earlier assumption that beta@ resolves to scot@lingolinq.com's Workspace inbox specifically; it also reaches this personal Gmail account, exact routing (group membership vs. a broader alias) not investigated further here. The message addressed directly to scotwahlquist@gmail.com was searched for across inbox/spam/trash (`in:anywhere`, `includeTrash:true`) and found nowhere -- reproducing the non-delivery exactly, now through ActionMailer rather than the raw SDK. This partially closes the 'was this just a raw-SDK artifact' question (adapter-level, not yet mailer-class-level) but does not change the underlying open root-cause question (still no per-message delivery event tracking exists to say why Gmail specifically drops it); remediation options (a)-(d) above remain the path forward. UPDATE 2026-07-11 (per-message event evidence, Scot's explicit go-ahead): ran scripts/gcp/phase5-ses-config-set-setup.sh live against lingolinq-prod (AWS account 239044785114, admin-mfa/wahlquist-admin MFA session) -- the missing SNS topic AllowSESPublish policy statement (the remediation built 2026-07-10) is now granted; queue/topic/subscription/configuration set already existed from the 2026-07-04 investigation. Reading the lingolinq-ses-events SQS queue returned two real per-message events for that exact MessageId: a Send event and a Delivery event (processingTimeMillis=865, smtpResponse="250 2.0.0 OK ... gsmtp", remoteMtaIp=74.125.135.26, reportingMTA=a27-57.smtp-out.us-west-2.amazonses.com). The non-arrival in scotwahlquist@gmail.com's inbox is therefore NOT an SES/LingoLinq sending-side failure; it narrows to Gmail-side post-acceptance handling (spam/promotions filtering, or similar) that the SES event pipeline has no visibility into. findings.title: UserExtra/UserLink profile-history caches are not invalidated when the source profile LogSession is deleted

remediation.options: Before extending any retention/purge job to LogSession log_type 'profile', add cache invalidation: when a 'profile' LogSession is destroyed, either recompute UserExtra#process_profile for the affected user_id/profile_id (dropping the deleted session from the recents list) or scrub matching entries by log_id from UserExtra.settings['recent_profiles'] and UserLink.data['state']['profile_history'] directly. Add a spec asserting the cache no longer contains the deleted log's summary/log_id after purge.

findings.notes: Surfaced by Codex's senior-dev review (/review-pr) of PR #535 (LL-1890f6a922, DataPolicyEnforcer retention scope): extending the retention purge to LogSession log_type 'profile' would delete the source record while UserExtra#process_profile's cached identifiable summary (template_id, summary, summary_color, log_id) and the mirrored UserLink.data['state']['profile_history'] entry are never refreshed on destroy, so identifiable content would persist in those caches after the source log is gone -- worse than the pre-existing status quo of not purging 'profile' at all. PR #535 responded by dropping 'profile' from DataPolicyEnforcer::RETAINABLE_LOG_TYPES (lib/data_policy_enforcer.rb) rather than shipping a half-fixed purge; this finding tracks the cache-invalidation work needed before 'profile' can safely be added back. Checked note/assessment/eval/journal for the same pattern: none found (user_badge.rb's assessment usage re-queries live LogSession rows on demand rather than caching a summary; weekly_stats_summary.rb caches only session_ids, not identifiable content, and per DATA_RETENTION.md's Analytics events row this is documented/accepted since aggregates 'do not re-identify individuals').

findings.title: DataPolicyEnforcer retention job skips child orgs that inherit (rather than set) a retention_months policy

remediation.options: Organization#effective_data_policy (app/models/organization.rb:81-101) is explicitly designed to inherit retention_months from a parent org, but enforce_retention!'s candidate-org WHERE clause only matches orgs whose OWN data_policy_version is > 0, and then only sweeps that org's own sponsored_users. A child org that never set its own policy (data_policy_version stays 0) is skipped by the WHERE clause entirely, even though its users are governed by an inherited window via a parent's policy -- so their communication logs never expire. Widen the candidate set to include any org whose effective (not just own) retention_months resolves to a positive value -- e.g. iterate every org with a policy-bearing ancestor, or drive the sweep off each org's own effective_data_policy rather than gating the WHERE clause on data_policy_version. Add a parent(policy)+child(data_policy_version 0) spec asserting the child's stale logs are purged.

findings.notes: Surfaced by adversary review of PR #535 (LL-1890f6a922, DataPolicyEnforcer log_type scope). Pre-existing since before that PR -- it changed only the log_type filter inside the loop, not the org-selection WHERE clause or the sponsored_users scoping -- but it directly undermines LL-1890f6a922's storage-limitation objective: an org hierarchy where only the parent sets retention_months leaves every child org's logs permanently unenforced. Confirmed against Organization#effective_data_policy's inheritance logic (organization.rb:84-96), which resolves retention_months from a parent for exactly this configuration, and against Organization#sponsored_users (organization.rb:677-685), which is scoped to one org's own attached users, not any descendant org's users.

findings.title: Retention purge deletes the LogSession's PaperTrail destroy-version and writes no disposal AuditEvent

remediation.options: Flusher.flush_record (lib/flusher.rb) destroys the record (creating a has_paper_trail :on => [:destroy] version, log_session.rb:24) and then immediately delete_alls that same version via flush_versions, and DataPolicyEnforcer.enforce_retention! writes no AuditEvent for its purges at all -- unlike Flusher.flush_leftovers, which records a per-category AuditEvent for its deletions (lib/flusher.rb ~line 224). This contradicts docs/legal/DATA_RETENTION.md row 30 (Authentication and audit trails / PaperTrail versions on User, Board, LogSession retained 6 years, HIPAA 45 CFR Sec 164.316(b)(2)(i)) and leaves no record proving what data was destroyed, when, or by which policy. Either stop deleting the destroy-version for LogSession specifically in this retention path (retain per row 30), or have enforce_retention! emit a per-run AuditEvent (actor 'system', org id, purged log ids/counts) the way flush_leftovers already does, so a HIPAA access-log review can reconstruct the disposal.

findings.notes: Surfaced by adversary review of PR #535 (LL-1890f6a922, DataPolicyEnforcer log_type scope). Pre-existing since before that PR -- Flusher.flush_record's destroy-then-delete-versions behavior and enforce_retention!'s lack of an AuditEvent call are both unchanged by it -- but PR #535 widens the set of log_types this same behavior applies to from 1 (session) to 4 (session/note/assessment/eval/journal), modestly increasing real-world exposure. No user impact today (prod/staging carry no real users, per project note), but this needs resolving before onboarding real school-district/hospital users, since the retention job is precisely the mechanism DATA_RETENTION.md documents as satisfying GDPR 5(1)(e) storage limitation, and doing so by destroying the very audit trail row 30 requires keeping for 6 years is an internal contradiction in the documented schedule, not just a code gap.

findings.title: Org retention policy purges a sponsored user's entire log history, including logs outside that org's context

remediation.options: Confirm with Scot whether an org's retention_months is meant to reach a sponsored user's entire log history (including logs predating enrollment, or generated under a personal/other-org context), or only logs created within that org's context. Today the query is user_id-scoped only, with no org/context filter, so any sponsoring org that sets retention_months deletes all of that user's aged logs regardless of origin -- for a user sponsored by more than one org, the most-aggressive policy effectively wins for their whole history. If the current behavior is intentional, document it explicitly in DATA_RETENTION.md's LogSession row rather than leaving it implicit; if not, scope the purge query by log ownership/context (e.g. author's org at the time, or a recorded originating-org field).

findings.notes: Surfaced by adversary review of PR #535 (LL-1890f6a922, DataPolicyEnforcer log_type scope). Pre-existing since before that PR -- the user_id-only scoping is unchanged, and PR #535 only widened the log_type filter -- but broadening the purge to 4 additional log_types (note/assessment/eval/journal) means more of a cross-context user's history is now reachable by this same scoping gap than before. This is data over-deletion risk, not a data leak, and is plausibly by design (retention as a property of the user's relationship to a sponsoring org); flagged as a design question for Scot rather than asserted as a defect.

findings.title: COPPA verifiable parental consent is granted with no immutable AuditEvent

remediation.options: On successful grant_parental_consent! completion emit an immutable AuditEvent (mirroring api/users#create school-authorization basis and closed supervisor-consent control LL-46fd4aa824) capturing user global_id, request IP, user-agent, grant timestamp and privacy_policy_version, so verifiable-consent record-keeping is tamper-evident and independent of the mutable user.settings coppa blob.

closureEvidence.verifierNote: Verified 2026-07-08: User#grant_parental_consent! now emits an immutable AuditEvent (event_type parental_consent_grant) atomically with the consent write inside with_lock(requires_new: true) -- an audit-insert failure rolls back the grant and the token stays retryable, and concurrent grants serialize. Payload carries method, ip, user_agent, privacy_policy_version, the persisted granted_at, and a stable record_id. Specs: spec/models/user_spec.rb (grant + rollback) and spec/controllers/parental_consents_controller_spec.rb. Remediated in #552 (merge 5ca663ad4).
closureEvidence.attestation: Scot Wahlquist 2026-07-08: attested verified-closed; remediated in #552, mirrors the canonical grant_ai_consent! atomic-audit pattern the finding called for.

findings.notes: Surfaced by privacy finder on 2026-07-08. COPPA 16 CFR 312.5 requires operators to obtain AND maintain records of verifiable parental consent. grant_parental_consent! (user.rb:385-423) records granted_at/policy_version only in the mutable settings JSON and calls self.save with no AuditEvent; the controller complete action writes none either. Codebase deliberately emits immutable AuditEvents for the parallel COPPA school-official exception (user.rb:1332 comment) and supervisor consent (LL-46fd4aa824 verified-closed), so this is an inconsistent gap on the most COPPA-central consent event. Distinct from LL-46fd4aa824 and eval-narrator-no-coppa-consent-gate. NEW. | adversary: confirmed -- no immutable AuditEvent on grant_parental_consent! (user.rb ~385-423) nor ParentalConsentsController#complete; contrast grant_ai_consent!/revoke_ai_consent! (user.rb:540,581) which each emit an AuditEvent. Nuance: User has_paper_trail :only [:settings,:user_name] (user.rb:44) DOES version the settings diff, but as a mutable versions-table row with nil whodunnit (unauthenticated email-link GET), so the no-IMMUTABLE-audit claim holds while no-audit-trail-at-all would overstate it.

findings.title: District seat reclaim converts an under-13's account to a consumer trial with no parental re-consent or notice (COPPA)

remediation.options: When Organization#remove_user calls License#release_user! (app/models/license.rb:53), a managed minor's account is set to managing_organization_id: nil + expires_at: 2.months.from_now and the org UserLink is removed, but no verifiable parental consent is captured and no parent/guardian notice is sent. District-created minors never had direct parental consent: the COPPA gate at user.rb:1321 is skipped for a validated org (org_authorized) under the FERPA/COPPA school-official exception, with a settings['school_authorization'] stamp standing in. So once the seat is reclaimed and the school authorization ends, continued direct-to-consumer processing of the child's data has no COPPA-valid basis (16 CFR 312.5); and, because the lawful basis then shifts to consent, no Art. 8-compliant under-16 parental-authorization mechanism for EU/Poland. Fix: at release_user!, if the account holder is a minor, set settings['coppa'] pending_parent_consent and email the guardian (school-created accounts often have no guardian email on file, so this likely needs a claim-based re-consent in which the family claims the account first, per outputs/plans/2026-07-09-offboarding-coppa-reconsent-fix-scope.md), reusing the existing grant_parental_consent! token flow in user.rb; gate continued processing on that consent, with export-then-delete if the guardian declines or the token expires. Distinct from the creation-time bypass tightening tracked in outputs/plans/2026-06-19-org-coppa-bypass-fix-scope.md.
remediation.timeframe: high 15-30d (before first real district student ages out or transfers)

closureEvidence.verifierNote:
CODE (origin/staging 8afabd1d2): Organization#remove_user (app/models/organization.rb:1064+) raises ArgumentError "offboarding birth month and year required" when JsonApi::Json.coppa_parental_consent_enabled? is true and the birth classification is nil, and calls user.begin_family_offboarding_consents!, so an under-13 is not silently converted to a consumer trial on seat reclaim. The automated path routes through the same consent start via License.expire_licenses!. Both present in the deployed production image (git show 73a8f6339).

CORRECTION 2026-08-30, raised by Codex review of PR #887 and INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED before acceptance: the 2026-08-29 closure note was WRONG to say only the birth-date requirement is flag-gated. The ENTIRE COPPA offboarding consent path is gated on JsonApi::Json.coppa_parental_consent_enabled?. Confirmed at four sites on origin/staging: User#requires_coppa_offboarding? returns false immediately (app/models/user.rb:513); begin_family_offboarding_consents! runs its COPPA branch only `if requires_coppa_offboarding?` (app/models/user.rb:576); User.process_expired_offboarding_consents! returns 0 immediately (app/models/user.rb:877); and Organization#remove_user gates on the flag directly (app/models/organization.rb:1071). With the flag OFF, Organization#remove_user still reclaims the seat while the parental re-consent path no-ops, i.e. the original defect recurs in full. The closure therefore rests ENTIRELY on the flag being enabled in production, not partially.

LIVE PRODUCTION READ (2026-08-30), which is what discharges that condition: executed as an audited `rails runner` on the lingolinq-prod Cloud Run job `lingolinq-migrate` (execution lingolinq-migrate-wbsw8, USER_KEY=scot@lingolinq.com, exit 0), against image 73a8f6339, the tag the serving web revision lingolinq-web-00024-yij runs. Result: coppa_parental_consent_enabled? => TRUE, unconditionally. Verbatim output: env_raw=nil, from_env=true, default_domain_value=true, enabled_no_req_ctx=true, custom_domains_total=0, explicit_setting=0, disabling_it=0, rails_env=production.

WHY UNCONDITIONAL (three independent reasons, any one sufficient): (1) JsonApi::Json.coppa_parental_consent_from_env? (lib/json_api/json.rb:202-207) returns false ONLY for an explicit 0/false/no/off, and ENV['COPPA_PARENTAL_CONSENT'] is unset on the serving revision - confirmed separately via `gcloud run services describe lingolinq-web`: absent from its 46 env vars, no secret volumes, no env-file mounts. (2) The only override path is a per-organization custom domain (load_domain, lib/json_api/json.rb:141-160) and production has ZERO custom domains, so every request resolves to default_domain. (3) SystemAppDefaults cannot reach the key: EDITABLE_FIELDS (lib/system_app_defaults.rb:4-10) is five fields, does not include coppa_parental_consent, and the merge is .slice()d to that list.

findings.title: Hard delete leaves UserVideo records and off-board voice recordings (ButtonSound) undeleted (GDPR right-to-erasure)

remediation.options: Flusher.flush_user_content / flush_user_completely (lib/flusher.rb:363-417) delete the user's Device, Utterance, NfcTag, UserIntegration, UserGoal, UserBadge, Webhook, UserBoardConnection, UserLink, LogSession and boards, but never sweep UserVideo (it appears only in transfer_user_content at line 354, a merge reassignment) or standalone ButtonSound by user_id. Message-bank voice recordings are ButtonSound rows keyed by user_id (button_sound.rb:128) and are removed only when attached to one of the user's own boards under full_flush (flusher.rb:264-276); off-board recordings and all UserVideo rows survive hard delete as orphaned S3-backed rows. The User model declares no has_many/dependent: :destroy for either (user.rb:16-23), so flush_record(user) cannot cascade. Fix: add UserVideo.where(user_id:) and ButtonSound.where(user_id:) sweeps to flush_user_content (deleting the backing S3 objects too), so a user-requested erasure removes the user's own recorded voice and video. Directly contradicts the docs/legal/COMPLIANCE_PROGRAM_OVERVIEW.md claim that deletion on request removes voice recordings.
remediation.timeframe: high 15-30d (right-to-erasure correctness; blocks the doc's deletion-removes-voice claim)

closureEvidence.verifierNote: Verified 2026-08-29 against origin/staging 8afabd1d2. lib/flusher.rb:394-406 sweeps both record types by user_id through flush_record, so the S3 remote_remove is scheduled rather than only the DB row deleted, with an in-code citation to this finding id. findings.title: Text-to-speech posts raw user text to subprocessors absent from the register (Abair has no DPA; Google TTS flow unrowed) (GDPR Art. 28/44)

remediation.options: Three TTS code paths post the text being spoken to an external provider with no PiiScrubber pass: lib/tts.rb#generate_irish (line 29-30) POSTs {text: text} to https://abair.ie/aac_irish (Trinity College Dublin / ADAPT academic endpoint), lib/tts.rb#generate_google (line 56-60) POSTs {input:{text:text}} to Google Cloud Text-to-Speech, and app/controllers/api/search_controller.rb:394-397 POSTs {input:{text:params['text']}} to the same Google endpoint. Board auto-sound generation routes through Tts.generate_audio. The spoken text is AAC utterance content that can contain a user's typed identifiers. Subprocessor gap: docs/legal/SUBPROCESSORS.md lists Google (Gemini API, #5) and Google Workspace (#12) but NO Google Text-to-Speech data flow, and does NOT list Abair/Trinity College Dublin at all, an undisclosed subprocessor with no DPA on file. Options: (1) add a Google TTS row and an Abair row to SUBPROCESSORS.md with the transfer basis (Google Cloud DPA covers the Google entity; Abair needs its own DPA/SCCs or a documented no-PII basis); (2) execute a DPA with the Abair operator or disable Irish TTS until one exists; (3) assess whether TTS text for COPPA-consent-pending children needs a consent gate or scrub before egress. The program overview's PII-scrubber sentence was scoped away from TTS in the same review (COMPLIANCE_PROGRAM_OVERVIEW.md, branch scot/compliance/right-sized-program-overview), which is disclosure, not remediation of the underlying subprocessor gap.

findings.title: Eval narration has no licensed-clinician gate (classified NOT a HIPAA Healthcare Activity)

remediation.options: No code gate required. Eval narration is adjudicated NOT a Healthcare Activity, so Anthropic Healthcare-Activity condition (iii) (licensed-clinician restriction) does not apply. If eval narration is ever repositioned as diagnosis, treatment, or auto-finalized clinical documentation, reopen this classification with Scot before PHI flows under that use.

disposition.rationale: The LingoLinq eval is an assistive-technology access / feature-match assessment (find-the-target tasks at progressively smaller grid sizes to a hit/miss heat map to a recommended board size and layout). The AI narrative summarizes access findings and the layout recommendation; it does not diagnose, treat, or produce charting/billing/coding/claims, so it is not one of Anthropic's enumerated Healthcare Activities and condition (iii) does not apply. Retained controls: Messages-API-only on the HIPAA-Ready org key, PII scrub + structural student-name drop + etiology minimization before egress, the EVAL_NARRATOR_MODEL allowlist, the COPPA gate, explicit per-request opt-in, and the org AI opt-out. See docs/legal/ANTHROPIC_BAA_ACCEPTED.md and the lib/eval_narrator.rb module header. Do not re-flag the absent licensed-clinician gate without first reopening this classification with Scot.

findings.title: Prod SES mail has no custom MAIL FROM domain, so SPF does not align with the From: domain and DMARC rests on DKIM alone; no Authentication-Results headers have ever been captured to confirm the SPF/DKIM/DMARC result on a delivered message

evidence.source: GCP cutover Gate 1 rehearsal (2026-07-19/20), Rehearsal step 3. A prod SES send via config set 'lingolinq-transactional' was ACCEPTED by SES and manual inbox receipt was confirmed, which closed the earlier delivery question (LL-42a24ee911, verified-closed). Two things that decision did NOT establish remain open: (a) the Authentication-Results headers on a delivered message were never captured, so the actual SPF/DKIM/DMARC evaluation result is unverified; (b) no custom MAIL FROM domain is configured, so the SPF-checked domain is the Amazon SES bounce domain rather than the From: domain, leaving SPF unaligned under DMARC and DKIM as the sole passing alignment mechanism. Verification was blocked in-session by a tooling mismatch, not a delivery failure: the mailtest targets the operator's personal mailbox while the available Gmail connector is authenticated as a Workspace user, so headers could not be read from that session.
evidence.snippet: No custom MAIL FROM domain on the prod SES identity; DMARC alignment carried by DKIM only. Authentication-Results header capture on a delivered prod message: not performed.

remediation.options: Before relying on prod SES for customer-facing transactional mail or alerting: (1) capture the Authentication-Results header from a delivered prod message and record the spf=/dkim=/dmarc= results as closure evidence -- read it from a mailbox the available connector can authenticate against, or via an SES configuration-set event destination (SNS / Firehose / EventBridge) rather than aggregate CloudWatch metrics; AND (2) configure a custom MAIL FROM subdomain on the SES identity with the required MX and SPF records so SPF aligns with the From: domain and DMARC no longer depends on DKIM alone. Not a Gate 1 DNS-cut blocker (accepted for Gate 1 by Scot, 2026-07-19); blocks treating prod mail as customer-ready.

findings.title: ButtonSound auto-uploads raw user VOICE-RECORDING audio to Google Cloud Speech-to-Text (speech:recognize) on every save, a data flow absent from the subprocessor register; audio cannot be PII-scrubbed (GDPR Art. 9/28/44, FERPA, COPPA)

remediation.options: ButtonSound#schedule_transcription (app/models/button_sound.rb:43-89) POSTs a base64-encoded copy of the user's recorded WAV button-sound to https://speech.googleapis.com/v1/speech:recognize, keyed by ENV['GOOGLE_TRANSLATE_TOKEN']. It is fired AUTOMATICALLY by the after_save :schedule_transcription hook (line 14) whenever a ButtonSound has a secondary_url and no transcription yet (schedule_once(:schedule_transcription, true), lines 86/89) -- no user action or consent step. The payload is a whole VOICE RECORDING (a communicator's or caregiver's actual voice), which is biometric-adjacent and may be GDPR Art. 9 special-category data, and cannot be run through lib/pii_scrubber.rb (the scrubber redacts text, not audio). Subprocessor gap: docs/legal/SUBPROCESSORS.md had no Google Cloud Speech-to-Text row before 2026-07-22. Options: (1) add the subprocessor row (done in DRAFT, #18) and record it in the change log; (2) confirm Speech-to-Text is a COVERED SERVICE under the existing Google Cloud BAA (§5.7) -- this is the primary control, since scrubbing is impossible for audio and the BAA is what makes raw covered-service processing permissible; (3) gate transcription behind a feature flag / disable_ai_features org opt-out, or behind COPPA consent, or disable it entirely until covered-service status is confirmed; (4) note it shares the GOOGLE_TRANSLATE_TOKEN with the translation flow (LL-c38e7da48e), so token liveness is already confirmed.

findings.title: Terms-agree modal is unreachable by switch scanning (no .modal_targets / .btn, opened without scannable)

evidence.snippet: <button type="button" class="la-btn la-btn--primary" {{on "click" (this.ctrlAction "confirm")}}>{{t "Agree and Continue" key="accept_and_continue"}}</button>

remediation.options: Two changes, both required. (1) In terms-agree.hbs, wrap the action buttons in a .modal_targets container and give each control the .btn class so the scanner selector at app/frontend/app/utils/modal.js:255 (".modal-dialog .modal_targets .btn, .modal-dialog .modal_targets a, ...") can find them. The existing la-btn / la-btn--primary / la-btn--ghost classes match none of those selectors. (2) Pass scannable: true at all four call sites: app/frontend/app/routes/index.js:123, index.js:132, app/frontend/app/routes/bento.js:51, bento.js:55 -- every one currently calls modal.open('terms-agree') with no options object, so scanning is never enabled for this modal even if the markup is fixed. Verify with a switch-scanning walkthrough, not markup inspection alone.

findings.notes: Discovered 2026-07-20 during VPC Phase 3 (EU AI Act Art.50 disclosure modal) planning, while cloning terms-agree as the acknowledge-gate exemplar. Independently confirmed against source by two agents plus the coordinator. PRE-EXISTING defect, not introduced by Phase 3; deliberately scoped OUT of Phase 3 so the Art.50 modal does not inherit the same gap (Phase 3's ai-disclosure component specifies .modal_targets + .btn + scannable: true as mechanically-checkable MUSTs). Impact is population-specific and severe: a switch-scanning AAC user -- a core LingoLinq user population -- cannot operate the Terms modal at all, and the modal is uncloseable, so the app is not merely degraded but unusable for them at that point. Rated high on that basis despite being a markup-level fix. WCAG 2.1 AA 2.1.1 Keyboard / 2.4.3 Focus Order operability.

findings.title: Terms-agree modal can be silently replaced by intro before the user agrees

remediation.options: In routes/index.js#setupController (and the parallel routes/bento.js path), the terms_agree-missing branch has no return, so execution falls through to modal.open('intro') when show_intro is set. On the synchronous fresh-model path that replaces terms-agree before it mounts (final currentTemplate is intro; utils/modal.js:138 and services/modal.js:92 resolve the first open with {replaced: true}). Fix by making the terms_agree gate authoritative: return after opening terms-agree, or defer intro until the terms-agree promise resolves with a genuine (non-replaced) result. Add a regression test covering really_fresh + show_intro true.

findings.notes: Discovered 2026-07-20 during VPC Phase 3 planning. Corrected 2026-07-23 after Codex review of PR #642: removed an inverted second-impact claim. CONSENT PRESENTATION (confirmed): when show_intro is true (set via routes/intro.js) and the fresh-model path opens terms-agree then intro in one run loop, Ember renders only the final currentTemplate (intro), so terms-agree never mounts and the user does not see or confirm Terms that visit; terms_agree stays false (no false-positive consent record). On the reload path, intro opens first — its init() clears show_intro and saves intro_watched — and the async reload may later open terms-agree. The previously claimed DURABLE WRITE LOSS / recurring intro (intro init skipped) does not occur: intro is the winner of the sync bump, not the victim. High rating remains for the consent-presentation gap on the sync path. PRE-EXISTING; scoped OUT of VPC Phase 3, which instead guards its own Art.50 chain against the bump by checking result.replaced rather than repairing this.

findings.title: Shared modal-dialog shell declares role=dialog aria-modal without aria-labelledby or aria-describedby

evidence.snippet: <div class="modal fade in" style="display: block;" data-uncloseable={{this.uncloseable}} role="dialog" aria-modal="true">

remediation.options: Add optional labelledBy / describedBy arguments to the modal-dialog component and bind them as aria-labelledby / aria-describedby on the dialog element. Ember omits a bound attribute whose value is undefined, so defaulting both to undefined is a verified no-op for the roughly 140 existing callers that do not pass them -- the change is additive and carries no regression risk to current modals. Then retrofit callers in priority order (terms-agree and any consent- or compliance-bearing modal first) so each dialog has a programmatically determined accessible name. WCAG 2.1 AA 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.

findings.notes: Discovered 2026-07-20 during VPC Phase 3 planning. PRE-EXISTING and system-wide (~140 callers). VPC Phase 3 adds the optional labelledBy/describedBy arguments to the shell as part of building its own ai-disclosure accessibility contract, but deliberately does NOT retrofit existing callers -- that retrofit is this finding and remains separate prioritized work. Rated medium rather than high because affected modals are still operable; the defect is that a screen-reader user gets no accessible name for the dialog, not that the dialog is unusable.

findings.title: No check asserts the Bedrock credential resolves to the BAA'd AWS account, so the AWS BAA's operative condition is an untested assumption

remediation.options: AiClient.build signs Bedrock with whatever credential pair is present and asserts nothing about which AWS account it belongs to. The AWS BAA (docs/legal/AWS_BAA_ACCEPTED.md) is scoped to a single account, and its stated operative condition is that Bedrock calls run under that account, so a credential from any other account would put PHI-bearing inference outside BAA coverage while every check in the repo stayed green. Add an explicit account assertion: call sts:GetCallerIdentity under the exact credential AiClient will use and compare Account against the BAA'd account id, ideally at deploy time in .github/workflows/deploy-cloudrun.yml as a post-deploy smoke step so a wrong credential fails the deploy rather than surfacing at first inference. A boot-time or first-call assertion that fails closed is an acceptable alternative or addition. Keep the account id in configuration, not hardcoded, so a future account migration is a config change. This is the control whose absence let an unverifiable verification claim stand in an attested compliance document from 2026-07-27 to 2026-08-01; PR 725 retracted the claim but did not add the control.

closureEvidence.verifierNote: Control built and merged via PR #768 (merge commit 9470ffbd7b15980c90c53b300148a8fdd6b8a2e3 into staging on 2026-08-10; ancestor-verified). AiClient now calls sts:GetCallerIdentity under the exact credential pair it will sign Bedrock with, against an endpoint pinned to https://sts.<region>.amazonaws.com, and refuses to return a client unless the returned Account equals BEDROCK_EXPECTED_AWS_ACCOUNT (lib/ai_client.rb:508 account_verified?, :570 verify_account, :450 sts_endpoint). It fails closed on mismatch, on any probe error, on a malformed expected-account value, and on a region string that is not a well-formed commercial AWS region: the region is interpolated into the STS hostname, so an unvalidated region would defeat the endpoint pin. The result is memoized per credential+region+expected fingerprint under a mutex with a 60s retry floor on failure and a monotonic clock, and the Puma warm-up at config/puma.rb:37 runs it after fork so a wrong credential surfaces at boot rather than at first inference. All four runtime AI seams gate on AiClient.available? and take a client via AiClient.build!, which raises NotAvailableError rather than returning nil (lib/ai_word_predictor.rb:59,201; lib/ai_board_generator.rb:555,568; lib/ai_prediction_generator.rb:118,238; lib/eval_narrator.rb:251,345). The account id stays in configuration rather than hardcoded, so an account migration is a config change; because an absent env var skips the assertion, the deploy pins it as a plaintext literal (.github/workflows/deploy-cloudrun.yml:273) and reads it back after deploy on both lingolinq-web and the lingolinq-worker worker pool, pinned to the value ^239044785114$ rather than to a 12-digit shape (:716-724, via scripts/gcp/assert-runtime-secrets.sh --required-literal). Covered by 69 examples in spec/lib/ai_client_spec.rb plus a new spec/lib/ai_prediction_generator_spec.rb for the seam that had no spec file at all. Confirmed independently out of band on 2026-08-10: a live sts:GetCallerIdentity under the production Bedrock credential returned account 239044785114, principal user/lingolinq-bedrock-runtime, which is the account docs/legal/AWS_BAA_ACCEPTED.md is scoped to. Three adversarial review rounds preceded merge and two returned BLOCK; the defects they caught were a redirectable STS endpoint, a readback that pinned shape instead of value, an unvalidated region, and a scheduled drift job that could never have authenticated (dropped, filed as issue #769). SCOPE NOTE: production runs main, so the assertion has not yet executed in a production process. Its first production execution emits the log line '[AiClient] Bedrock credential verified against AWS account 239044785114' and lands on the next staging-to-main release, which auto-deploys under #758.
closureEvidence.attestation: Scot Wahlquist 2026-08-11: attested verified-closed. The automated account assertion this finding asked for is built, test-covered, and merged to staging in #768, and the production Bedrock credential was independently confirmed to resolve to the BAA'd account 239044785114. What remains is deployment, not construction; the production log line is being watched as deploy confirmation, not as evidence the control exists.

disposition.rationale: Closed on the control's existence and test coverage rather than on its first production execution, because the finding is that no check asserts the account and that is no longer true at staging head. Reaching production is tracked as a release watch item on the next staging-to-main merge, not as an open finding.

findings.notes: Promoted from PR #725 review (adversary) on 2026-08-02. Filed from the PR 725 correction of docs/legal/AWS_BAA_ACCEPTED.md. It becomes live the moment credentials are mounted (PR 719).' That activation condition WAS met.
