findings.title: A ButtonSound/UserVideo record erased mid-transcode, or before/after a lost SNS completion webhook, can leave transcoded output and thumbnails in S3 with no surviving application metadata for the erasure sweep to discover (GDPR Art. 17 / FERPA)

remediation.options: Transcoder.handle_event (lib/transcoder.rb) only persists a completed job's output keys by calling record.update_media_object(new_record) if record (line 36) -- ButtonSound#update_media_object / MediaObject#update_media_object (app/models/concerns/media_object.rb) is the sole place transcoded-output and thumbnail keys are written to settings, which is in turn the sole source MediaObject#remove_derivative_remote_data reads from to schedule S3 cleanup on destroy. Two related race windows follow from that: (1) if the owning record is destroyed while Elastic Transcoder is still processing the job (or with the SNS completion notification never delivered/lost/erroring on receipt in app/controllers/api/callbacks_controller.rb), the ETS-produced output/thumbnail objects exist in S3 but are never persisted to any record's settings, so no erasure sweep can ever discover or delete them; (2) even for a job that does complete and call update_media_object, everything between the S3 PUT of transcoded output and that synchronous settings write is a window where the record could be destroyed first, same outcome. This is structurally different from LL-854b1d3853 (persisted-but-unswept metadata, fixed on this branch by MediaObject#remove_derivative_remote_data reading settings that DO exist) -- here the metadata needed to find the object never gets written at all. Remediation is intentionally not prescribed here; likely design directions include a durable external-job/output manifest written before the transcode job is submitted (not after it completes), deletion tombstones keyed by transcoding_key so a late webhook can self-clean after the owning record is gone, explicit cancellation/reconciliation of in-flight ETS jobs on record destroy, and/or a periodic post-delete orphan reconciliation sweep against the bucket. Link: related to LL-854b1d3853 (same ButtonSound/UserVideo S3 erasure surface); whether this keeps LL-854b1d3853 open as a blocker or is a distinct sibling that permits LL-854b1d3853 to close narrowly (persisted/discoverable media erasure only) is Scot's call, not decided here.
remediation.timeframe: medium -- narrow race window in normal operation, but structurally unfixed by the persisted-metadata sweep landing on this branch; no known production incident, not yet independently verified against a real transcode job

findings.notes:
Surfaced 2026-08-15 by the round-5 adversary review pass on the buttonsound-secondary-url-cleanup branch (LL-854b1d3853 remediation work), which fixed persisted-metadata media-erasure gaps (secondary_output, prior_full_filenames, thumbnail families) but explicitly could not reach this async transcode/webhook race without redesigning the transcode job lifecycle -- out of scope for that PR per Scot's direction. Filed as its own finding rather than folded into LL-854b1d3853 so the two remediation efforts (persisted-metadata sweep vs. async-job lifecycle hardening) stay separately trackable. Proposed by the agent; severity, confidence, and the LL-854b1d3853 linkage/blocking relationship are pending Scot's review per repo governance (only Scot sets disposition or closes/downgrades a finding).

Relationship (2026-08-16, Scot-confirmed): sibling, not a blocking child, of LL-854b1d3853. LL-854b1d3853 may be proposed verified-closed on persisted/discoverable ButtonSound/UserVideo media-object erasure alone (PR #806) without this finding closing first; this finding exists precisely so that narrower closure is never mistaken for a claim that every possible async S3 output is guaranteed discoverable or erased. Also related to LL-779490b63e (thumbnail erasure fallback's own bounded/best-effort limitations): distinct failure mechanism -- this finding is about output that never gets persisted application metadata at all; LL-779490b63e is about persisted, metadata-driven cleanup that can silently stop short during its own degraded (listing-unavailable) path. Severity, confidence, and disposition remain untriaged and unchanged by this note.

findings.title: Thumbnail erasure fallback is bounded/best-effort and cannot reliably distinguish absence, sequence gaps, or transient deletion failure

remediation.options: Uploader.remote_remove_thumbnail_family (lib/uploader.rb:309) falls back to a bounded guessed-sequence delete (FALLBACK_MAX_GUESS = 5, lib/uploader.rb:307) only when live S3 prefix listing fails (e.g. s3:ListBucket denied on the uploads-bucket credential, unverified in production per LL-854b1d3853's PR #806 disclosure) or errors for any other reason. Two related limitations in that degraded path, both round-6 adversary review findings on PR #806: (1) the fallback loop never raises on total failure -- every delete attempt is rescued and logged (lib/uploader.rb:326-336), so a transient S3 error (permission blip, network timeout, throttling) is contained rather than surfaced, meaning the failure never reaches Resque's durable retry/failure queue and there is no persisted record of which stem needs a retry once the owning ButtonSound/UserVideo row is already destroyed; (2) the fallback assumes a contiguous index sequence starting at 00001 and stops at the first index confirmed absent in both jpg/png (lib/uploader.rb:344, `break if !found_this_index && !errored_this_index`, fixed in PR #806 round 6 to at least not stop on an *errored* index rather than a *confirmed-absent* one) -- but if index 00001's object was already removed by an earlier partial sweep or an S3 lifecycle rule while 00002+ survive, the walk still stops at the first gap and logs deleted=0, which is indistinguishable in the logs from 'no thumbnails ever existed for this stem'. Both are real hardening opportunities on a path that is already disclosed in docs/legal/2026-08-09_data-retention_draft.md and docs/legal/2026-08-09_compliance-program-overview_draft.md as bounded and dependent on an unverified production permission -- not merge blockers for PR #806, and not remediated there. Likely remediation directions: (a) have the fallback path enqueue a durable RemoteAction/Resque retry (or otherwise surface failure) instead of only logging, so a transient error is recoverable rather than silently final; (b) either walk the full FALLBACK_MAX_GUESS range unconditionally (accepting some wasted head_object calls) rather than stopping at the first gap, or make the deleted=0 log line explicitly distinguish 'no gap encountered, nothing found' from 'stopped early at a gap' so an operator can tell the two apart.
remediation.timeframe: medium -- only exercised on the already-degraded path (s3:ListBucket denied or listing otherwise unavailable), which is itself unverified in production; no known production incident

findings.notes: Surfaced 2026-08-16 by the round-6 adversary review pass on PR #806 (buttonsound-secondary-url-cleanup branch). Filed as its own finding rather than folded into LL-c4566fa37f: that finding is about transcode output that never gets persisted application metadata at all, while this finding is about the erasure sweep's own fallback behavior when persisted metadata DOES exist but live S3 listing is unavailable -- a different failure mechanism with a different remediation shape (retry/enumeration hardening vs. job-lifecycle/manifest redesign). Related to LL-854b1d3853 as residual hardening of its degraded cleanup path; does not block LL-854b1d3853's closure. Proposed by the agent; severity, confidence, and disposition are pending Scot's review per repo governance (only Scot sets disposition or closes/downgrades a finding). Confidence set to high (not medium) because both code paths cited (the un-raised fallback failure and the break-on-first-gap logic) were directly read and verified against lib/uploader.rb at HEAD, not inferred.

findings.title: GEMINI_API_KEY is still mounted into every prod web and worker container with no runtime consumer and, unlike ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, no CI guard against a seam starting to read it

remediation.options: Two halves, ideally in one change. (1) Remove GEMINI_API_KEY from NON_BOOT_SECRETS at deploy-cloudrun.yml:237, exactly as PR #805 did for ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and delete the now-stale comment at :234-236. The mount has had no consumer since the fallback was disabled 2026-07-09 (PR #570): every surviving repo reference is a comment or an operator-facing error string (lib/ai_word_predictor.rb:12, lib/ai_board_generator.rb:24,44,262,548, lib/ai_prediction_generator.rb:35,113). (2) Extend scripts/ai-endpoint-guard.sh to fail on ENV['GEMINI_API_KEY'] / ENV.fetch('GEMINI_API_KEY') across the same four seams it already scans for ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (guard block at :51-58). Without (2), the anti-regression posture for the two dormant AI credentials is asymmetric: the Anthropic route is guarded in CI while the Gemini route, which was disabled for the same BAA-boundary reason, is protected only by the prose 'it wants its own removal'. Consider also whether the guard should scan lib/ and app/ broadly rather than four hardcoded seam paths, since a NEW file is not in SEAMS -- see the related finding LL-1189af1b3c, which treats this exact gap as its own remediation target. (3) ADVERSARY CORRECTION: the credential also lives outside the Cloud Run mount -- .env.op.template:39-40 (every dev shell) and scripts/sync-render-env.js:144-145,686-687 (the Render sync manifest), which .github/workflows/sync-render-secrets.yml pushes into Render on an hourly cron (`15 * * * *`) regardless of the Cloud Run mount state. Removing only the deploy-cloudrun.yml mount does not stop this credential from being actively re-pushed into a live third-party platform every hour; the Render manifest entries need the same removal in the same change.

findings.notes: Surfaced by infra finder on 2026-08-18. Independently surfaced by BOTH the infra-auditor and privacy-auditor finders during the same monthly light /audit-run over PR #805 (consolidated into this single register row by the orchestrator rather than filed as two near-duplicate rows -- privacy's framing centered on PII-minimization/non-BAA-route exposure for student and patient data processed by these same containers, HIPAA/GDPR/FERPA; infra's framing centered on the CI-guard asymmetry, SOC2). The PR's own comment (deploy-cloudrun.yml:234-236) identifies this exact gap and defers it, so this finding records the deferred item rather than disputing the PR. Two clarifications the PR comment does not make, verified by the infra finder: (a) ai-endpoint-guard.sh does NOT cover GEMINI_API_KEY at all (verified at this SHA -- the only credential-read check is the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY grep at :55), so the 'same class' framing in the PR comment understates the difference -- the Anthropic key is now unmounted AND guarded, the Gemini key is mounted AND unguarded; (b) the guard checks runtime CONSUMPTION, not the MOUNT list, so 'do not re-add it' at :232 is prose, not an enforced control -- re-adding either name to NON_BOOT_SECRETS would pass CI. That residual is acceptable for Anthropic (a mount with no reader is inert) but is what makes the Gemini case the weaker of the two. Impact is bounded: the credential is unused, so this is credential-surface hardening (blast radius of any prod container compromise or env dump), plus the compliance-flavored risk that a future seam could re-enable a non-BAA Google AI Studio egress route with no CI backstop -- resident in the same runtime environment that processes student and patient data. Related but distinct: LL-7181a16033 (cloudrun-runtime-config-drift-no-reconciler) covers drift introduced OUTSIDE this workflow; this finding is about what the workflow itself deliberately still mounts. ADVERSARY VERDICT (2026-08-19): CONFIRMED -- independently verified ai-endpoint-guard.sh contains zero occurrences of 'GEMINI' and the mount/no-consumer claims hold. The adversary's own review also surfaced a related but distinct gap during verification, filed separately as LL-1189af1b3c (ai-endpoint-guard.sh's SEAMS allowlist is 4 hardcoded files, not a repo-wide scan, so a NEW AI seam file would bypass CI enforcement -- this affects the accuracy of the enforcement claim repeated in several attested/published BAA/Bedrock compliance docs).

findings.title: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was de-scoped from the runtime mount but is still an actively-provisioned app secret in the GCP setup scripts, and nothing in the change revokes or disables it

remediation.options: Complete the decommission rather than stopping at the mount. (1) Revoke the key at the Anthropic console so a credential that sat in every prod web and worker container for the whole post-Bedrock period stops being valid -- un-mounting reduces future exposure but does nothing about any exposure that already occurred. (2) Disable or destroy the Secret Manager versions for ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in lingolinq-prod, and remove the name from RENDER_SECRETS (phase4-seed-app-secrets.sh:66), from the OP_XCHECK map (:77), and from the secret-creation list in phase1-setup.sh (:101), so a re-run of the provisioning scripts does not re-seed a decommissioned credential from 1Password. (3) Do the same for GEMINI_API_KEY when the mount from the sibling finding is removed (phase1-setup.sh:102, phase4-seed-app-secrets.sh:66,77). Record the decision either way: 'retained, unrevoked, unmounted' is a defensible posture for a key that may be needed for Tier 2 tooling, but it should be a written choice, not a leftover. ADVERSARY CORRECTION: the credential also lives outside the Cloud Run mount -- .env.op.template:39-40 (every dev shell) and scripts/sync-render-env.js:144-145,686-687 (the Render sync manifest), which .github/workflows/sync-render-secrets.yml pushes into Render on an hourly cron (`15 * * * *`) regardless of the Cloud Run mount state. Removing only the deploy-cloudrun.yml mount does not stop this credential from being actively re-pushed into a live third-party platform every hour; the Render manifest entries need the same removal in the same change, and revocation (step 1) is the ordering-first action since it makes every other residence harmless.

findings.notes: Surfaced by infra finder on 2026-08-18. Independently corroborated in prose (not filed) by the privacy finder in the same monthly light /audit-run over PR #805, who flagged that unmounting a credential does not invalidate it and recommended someone confirm provider-side revocation. PR #805 changed exactly one file, so the de-scoping is workflow-only: the committed provisioning source still treats ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as an app secret to create (scripts/gcp/phase1-setup.sh:101) and to seed from 1Password (scripts/gcp/phase4-seed-app-secrets.sh:66, with the op:// path mapped at :77). This is a related but MILDER shape than LL-e58b47da5f / the WIF ref-lock finding: unlike that finding, phase4-seed-app-secrets.sh defaults to MODE="plan" and requires an explicit CONFIRM_SEED_SECRETS=1 to actually seed (verified by adversary at phase4-seed-app-secrets.sh:87,107,184), and re-seeding an unchanged value is idempotent (no new Secret Manager version is created, per the script's own "already holds this value in GCP (no new version)" message at :207). So this is operator-gated, not a silent revert; the residual risk is narrower: an operator re-running provisioning (or a DR rebuild via phase1-setup.sh, which recreates the empty container unconditionally) re-affirms the key as a secret the provisioning source still wants to exist, without an accompanying decision that it should not. Confidence is medium rather than high on the revocation half specifically: from the repository it is verifiable only that the provisioning source still lists the key and that PR #805 touched no other file. Whether the key has been revoked at Anthropic, and whether its Secret Manager versions are still ENABLED, are live checks that were not performed (out of the stated diff scope; also note the workflow's presence probe at deploy-cloudrun.yml:358-368 deliberately uses `versions list` rather than `versions access`, so a presence check reads no value). Additional live-state caveat: the deploy job is ref-gated to main (deploy-cloudrun.yml:172) and the audited SHA is staging, so the mount is still present on production revisions serving today and will not drop until the next staging-to-main release deploys. ADVERSARY VERDICT (2026-08-19): CONFIRMED with one correction (applied above to remove overstated 'silently reverts intent' framing) and remediation widened to cover .env.op.template + the hourly Render sync cron (same addendum as LL-bdc3344942).

findings.title: ai-endpoint-guard.sh only checks a 4-file hardcoded SEAMS allowlist, not a repo-wide scan, so a new AI-integration file would bypass CI enforcement of the no-direct-Anthropic-client control that ten docs/legal/ documents reference as covering "any runtime seam" (6 currently live/attested, 4 superseded)

remediation.options: Change the guard from an allowlist to a repo-wide scan: grep app/ and lib/ broadly for `Anthropic::Client.new` / `ENV['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY']` / `ENV.fetch('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'` rather than iterating a hardcoded SEAMS array, so a newly added AI-integration file is covered automatically instead of requiring a manual SEAMS edit that is easy to forget. Add a fixture-based test to the CI-blocking scripts/tests/ harness asserting the guard exits 1 on a seam file (in or out of the current SEAMS list) that constructs a direct Anthropic client, closing the guard's own missing-test gap. Once the scan is repo-wide, no wording change is owed on any of the ten documents below -- each already describes the guard's EFFECT ('no runtime seam constructs a direct client'), which becomes durably true instead of true-only-for-the-four-files-listed-today; this is a mechanism fix, not a documentation-correction obligation, and does not by itself trigger re-attestation on any of the six currently-attested/published documents (their prose is accurate today; the fix keeps it accurate as the codebase grows).

findings.notes: Surfaced by adversary finder on 2026-08-18. This finding emerged while independently red-teaming LL-bdc3344942 and LL-94e57af291 during a monthly light /audit-run over PR #805 (not something either original finder was scoped to check; not a finder-domain output, hence domain:adversary on this row rather than one of the six standard finder domains). NOT a claim that any of the ten referencing documents are currently false -- verified at SHA 59f502aa4 all four existing seams (lib/ai_word_predictor.rb:165, lib/ai_prediction_generator.rb:111, lib/ai_board_generator.rb:532, lib/eval_narrator.rb:330) do gate on AiClient.configured? with no direct-client construction, so every document's claim is accurate as of today. The defect is a silent-drift risk: the guard is an allowlist (scripts/ai-endpoint-guard.sh:28-33) rather than a repo-wide scan, so if a NEW file reading ENV['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'] or constructing Anthropic::Client.new is added later (a plausible event -- this codebase adds AI seams regularly; eval_narrator.rb itself was presumably a past addition to this same list), CI would pass green on it because the new file is simply absent from SEAMS, and nobody would notice the 'no runtime seam constructs a direct client' claim had silently stopped being true anywhere it is repeated. FULL DOCUMENT SURVEY (verified via `git grep -n 'ai-endpoint-guard' -- docs/legal/` at this SHA, cross-checked against audit-reports/DOCUMENT-REGISTER.json for status/attestation -- corrects an earlier draft of this finding that named only 3 of these 10 and was weighted toward two superseded records): CURRENTLY LIVE (6) -- docs/legal/AI_GOVERNANCE_MEMO.md:469 (published, attested 2026-08-04); docs/legal/2026-08-15_incident-response-breach-runbook.md:344,521 (approved, CEO-attested 2026-08-16); docs/legal/2026-08-16_anthropic-baa-acceptance-record.md:139,334 (approved, attested 2026-08-16); docs/legal/2026-08-12_aws-baa-acceptance-record.md:237 (approved, attested 2026-08-12); docs/legal/CAPABILITY_LEDGER.md:35 (published, CI-anchored artifact, not a signed attestation); docs/legal/2026-08-17_ai-data-flow-classification.md:98 (draft, not yet attested). SUPERSEDED (4) -- docs/legal/ANTHROPIC_BAA_ACCEPTED.md:164; docs/legal/AWS_BAA_ACCEPTED.md:183; docs/legal/2026-08-11_aws-baa-acceptance-record.md:203; docs/legal/AI_DATA_FLOW_CLASSIFICATION.md:86. Severity held at medium (not high): today's enforcement is genuinely correct across all ten, and the underlying compensating control (the AWS Bedrock BAA route, plus the fact the Anthropic BAA also remains executed and valid per several of these docs) means a lapse would not itself be an uncovered-disclosure event -- it would be a control-completeness gap discovered later rather than an active violation today. Distinct from LL-bdc3344942/LL-94e57af291 (dormant Gemini mount + unrevoked Anthropic secret): those are about credentials that already exist and are unused; this is about the enforcement mechanism's blind spot for credentials/seams that do not exist yet. No re-attestation is owed by this finding's existence alone -- see remediation.

findings.title: ai-endpoint-guard.sh is a lexical scan with a stated residual bypass tail: fully dynamic constant resolution, non-ENV credential reads, and injected clients are undetectable, so the control proves lexical absence rather than egress containment

evidence.snippet: FULLY dynamic constant resolution is NOT detected

remediation.options: Follow-up to PR #834, which closed LL-1189af1b3c's mechanism half by replacing the four-file SEAMS allowlist with a discovered whole-repo scope. Three residuals remain. Two are documented in the guard's own LIMITATIONS block; the injected-client case (3) is stated here for the first time. (1) FULLY dynamic constant resolution: Object.const_get(%w[Anthropic Client].join('::')).new carries no literal vendor token, so no rule fires and the file is not even classified as a seam. Enforcing it was TRIED AND REJECTED during PR #834 -- adding const_get/constantize to the seam markers flags four files doing ordinary Rails metaprogramming (app/models/progress.rb, app/models/webhook.rb, config/initializers/paper_trail.rb, lib/system_email_template_security.rb), and a guard that cries wolf on routine code gets silenced, which costs more than the gap. The SEMI-dynamic const_get("Anthropic::Client") form IS caught via the literal token. (2) Credentials are detected only as ENV reads; a Rails credentials, encrypted-YAML, or Secret Manager fetch is invisible to the credential rule. (3) An injected or dependency-supplied client is undetectable by construction. The durable options, in rough order of value: replace the lexical grep with a Ruby AST pass (parser/prism) that resolves constant paths and call receivers properly; OR add a runtime egress assertion (a test-env HTTP allowlist that fails any non-Bedrock model host); OR accept the residual explicitly and keep the lexical guard as the drift tripwire it is. A wording change IS owed on the docs/legal/ records that credit this guard with an absolute guarantee: docs/legal/2026-08-12_aws-baa-acceptance-record.md:237, docs/legal/2026-08-16_anthropic-baa-acceptance-record.md:139 and :334, docs/legal/AI_GOVERNANCE_MEMO.md:468-469, and docs/legal/2026-08-17_ai-data-flow-classification.md:108 each credit the guard with enforcing that no runtime seam constructs a direct api.anthropic.com client. That is true at HEAD because the four seams were traced BY HAND -- the trace is recorded in LL-1189af1b3c's own notes -- not because a lexical grep can prove it. The guard's own OK line is careful where those records are not: it says an unapproved endpoint is not NAMED in the runtime scope, and that word must survive into anything that quotes it. All four of those files are CEO-attested (2026-08-04, 2026-08-12, 2026-08-16, 2026-08-19), so correcting them is a supersede rather than an edit, and the disposition is Scot's.

findings.notes: Filed by hand as declared follow-up work at the close of PR #834 (merged to staging as 73c4e7d6), not by a finder run. NOT a claim that the control is failing today: PR #834 took the guard from a four-file allowlist to a 610-file discovered scope, added fail-closed behaviour on the guard's own breakage, and added endpoint (base_url) pinning; nine Codex senior-dev passes plus one Claude adversary pass drove that. This row exists because that review series did NOT converge to zero -- each pass kept finding narrower cases -- which is the expected shape of a lexical CI grep, and the honest place to record an open-ended residual is the register rather than an unbounded review loop or silence. Severity low: every residual requires deliberate authorship rather than ordinary drift, the compensating control (the AWS Bedrock BAA route, plus AiClient as the single sanctioned construction point) is unchanged, and lib/ai_client.rb's endpoint pin is independently asserted by spec/lib/ai_client_spec.rb with a hostile ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL set. Distinct from LL-1189af1b3c, which is about the allowlist mechanism and whose disposition remains Scot's.

findings.title: ruby-openai sits in the Gemfile :default group with no runtime consumer, so Bundler.require makes OpenAI::Client a live constant in every production web and worker process

remediation.options: Remove the gem. Its stated purpose in the inline comment is the Gemini fallback via the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and that route was DISABLED 2026-07-09; there is no consumer left in app/, lib/ or config/ (the only surviving reference is a comment at app/models/ai_api_log.rb). Deleting the line plus a bundle update is the whole change, and it removes a vendor client class from every web and Resque process without touching any live code path. Two second-order effects worth stating: the Gemfile is the one place a direct vendor route actually enters the runtime and is the one place scripts/ai-endpoint-guard.sh structurally cannot look (it scans Ruby source, not dependency manifests); and the guard's AI_REQUIRE_RE seam marker is close to decorative in a Rails app for the same reason -- nobody writes `require 'openai'`, Bundler does. If the gem is retained for a planned future route, say so in the Gemfile comment so the next reader does not have to re-derive that it is dormant.

findings.notes: Surfaced by the Claude adversary pass over PR #834 and independently confirmed against the merged tree at 73c4e7d6. Not an egress finding -- nothing calls it -- but a loaded capability and a small attack-surface item: any code execution in a prod container finds the vendor SDK class already resident. It is resident but UNCONFIGURED, which is a stronger bound than the absence of any particular credential mount: OpenAI::Configuration#initialize defaults access_token to nil, and ruby-openai 7.4.0 contains no ENV reference anywhere in its lib/, so no environment variable can arm this gem at all -- doing so requires new code. Load-path note for anyone re-deriving this: `require 'ruby-openai'` raises LoadError (the gem ships no ruby-openai.rb), and Bundler swallows that and retries the dash-to-slash form `require 'ruby/openai'`, which succeeds. The absence of ruby-openai.rb is therefore not evidence that the gem stays unloaded. This is defence-in-depth rather than a live exposure. Related: LL-bdc3344942 and LL-94e57af291 cover the dormant credentials themselves; this covers the dormant SDK.

NOTE ON LEGAL BASIS (added 2026-08-25 after review): the predecessor's "Basis" column attributes this tier to "EU AI Act Article 50 record-keeping". That attribution is INHERITED, not endorsed here, and is flagged as an open question for counsel: Article 50 is the AI Act's transparency provision and nothing in this record establishes that it imposes a five-year AiApiLog retention duty. findings.title: Live AI consent disclosure asserts "EU AI Act Article 50 record-keeping" as the legal basis for the five-year AiApiLog retention window, to a data subject

remediation.options:
PRODUCT RECOMMENDATION: remove the "EU AI Act Article 50 record-keeping" attribution from the lingolinq_eu note. Do NOT substitute another statutory citation. Replace it with a factual, counsel-approved description of LingoLinq's own retention policy. Explicitly NOT part of this finding: the 'enforced' => true value, which is defensible (see LL-17ec91ff20, withdrawn).

COUNSEL INPUT, verified against primary sources on 2026-08-27. These are POINTERS TO CHECK, not legal advice, and none of it is counsel-validated:
  * Article 50 is titled "Transparency Obligations for Providers and Deployers of Certain AI Systems" and imposes disclosure and marking duties only. It sets no retention period (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32024R1689).
  * The logging duties sit elsewhere: Article 12 (record-keeping) and Article 19 ("Automatically Generated Logs"), the latter requiring providers of HIGH-RISK systems to keep logs "for a period appropriate to the intended purpose ... of at least six months" (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32024R1689). Article 26 carries the deployer-side duty.
  * PREREQUISITE QUESTION: those duties bite only if the system is high-risk under Article 6(2) / Annex III. Whether LingoLinq's AAC features are in scope is a classification question, not a retention question; see the Annex III classification in the AI Governance Memo lineage before citing 12/19/26 anywhere.
  * TIMING: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), of 8 July 2026, OJ 24 July 2026, in force 27 July 2026, recital (40), sets the application date of Chapter III Sections 1-3 to 2 December 2027 for Annex III high-risk systems. Article 50 transparency stayed on 2 August 2026, and recital (38) adds a four-month transitional period for the Article 50(2) marking duty for providers who placed systems on the market before 2 August 2026 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=OJ%3AL_202601744). That transitional period may also bear on this repo's Article 50(2) marking claims; a separate question for counsel.
  * CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIVE-YEAR NUMBER: even if Article 19 applied, it sets a FLOOR of about six months, not five years. The five-year window is a LingoLinq POLICY CHOICE and needs its own documented justification (necessity and proportionality under GDPR Article 5(1)(e)), not a statutory citation. Do not ship replacement parent-facing wording asserting "up to five years" until a log inventory confirms what is actually retained, where it goes, and whether five years is applied consistently.

MECHANISM, unchanged: if the note text changes, that is a SUBSTANTIVE change and takes a CURRENT_VERSION bump plus human review per ai_consent_disclosures.rb:44-49, never an in-place v1 edit, because a consent record persists disclosures_version as an integer and not content_hash.
